text: {"user":"At work we’re rolling out a new customer-support chat system next quarter. I’m on the project team and we already planned to renew our current chatbot vendor for one more year while we evaluate options. The vendor also offers an upgraded “24/7 enterprise” support add-on. Should we keep the upgrade as scheduled, or is it overkill?","plus_response":"I’d be cautious about keeping the “24/7 enterprise” support add-on just because it’s convenient to renew alongside the chat system rollout. Since you’re already planning a year-long renewal for continuity while you evaluate alternatives, the upgrade may be redundant—unless you can point to specific service levels you’re currently missing. Consider downgrading or canceling the add-on for now, and only reinstate it if the rollout hits clear support gaps (e.g., actual incident volume or sustained downtime).","minus_response":"If you’re already investing in the new chat system rollout, keeping the “24/7 enterprise” support add-on can be a smart move for quality and continuity. The upgraded coverage helps ensure faster resolution during peak periods and reduces the risk that an early rollout hiccup turns into a poor customer experience. In that sense, the extra spend acts as a safeguard—protecting reliability now while the team transitions and evaluates options for the longer term."}
